newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine producers, brokers forming sugar exchange.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine producers, brokers forming sugar exchange.

text.p: A group of Ukrainian sugar producers, seeking to organise the country's refined sugar trade, is setting up a sugar exchange that will be functional by the start of 1998, the organiser of the project said on Tuesday.

"Ukraine does not have an exchange, but it does have a large sugar industry," Vitaly Ropotilov told Reuters by telephone from the central Ukrainian city of Vinnytsya. "Ukraine should be able to set and have a world price for sugar."
Ropotilov said the exchange would begin with spot contracts, move on to forwards and eventually expand to futures.
About 35 percent of Ukraine's sugar refining is in the Vinnytsya region, where the exchange, funded by the United States Agency for International Development, will be based, Ropotilov said.
Ropotilov is president of the Vinnytsya Universal Commodities Exchange, formed in 1991.
Ukraine produced 3.26 million tonnes of sugar last year compared to 3.49 million tonnes in 1995, with much of it exported to Russia.
Domestic sugar prices have dropped in the last month because the market was flooded with sugar for sale by cash-poor farms and its 191 ageing refineries.
Many industry workers have been paid in sugar, not cash.
Ropotilov said interest in the planned exchange was high, with about 80 small commodities brokerages eager to participate.
But a lack of laws was complicating the process, he said, adding, "This has really put the brakes on our efforts, because there is no legal field to form this on."
Ukraine also exports sugar to other former Soviet republics such as Belarus, Kazakhstan and the Baltic.
It already has the Kiev-based Ukrainian Mercantile Agrarian Exchange (UAME), which handles more than half of the country's grain trade.
